title: Atomic Spend Lens: Compact Export & Pricing Preset Patterns
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and prototype a compact, role-aware token-level cost analytics panel (the 'Atomic Spend Lens') inside Redwood Console. The lens should let users: 1) view per-invocation and per-token breakdowns with attribution to routes, models, and prompts; 2) export condensed records for chargeback and accounting (CSV/NDJSON) optimized for downstream billing systems; 3) apply and preview pricing presets (slab, tiered, and per-token overrides) and estimate invoice impact in-line; 4) present a mobile-friendly compact row format and an expanded detailed modal for forensic workflows. Emphasis on minimal cognitive load for platform and finance users while preserving traceability for SREs and engineers. Work includes hi-fi prototypes, annotated spec for engineers, and a short usability checklist for validation sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Token-level rows show: timestamp, route id, model variant, invocation tokens, input tokens, output tokens, effective unit price, line cost, and quick-link to full trace
Compact row condenses to <= 7 visible columns in Console list view while preserving an expandable detail panel
Export supports: aggregated CSV (daily/hourly granularity), raw NDJSON (one event per invocation with tokens metadata), and a chargeback-ready flat CSV mapping to accounting dimension columns
Pricing presets allow: base per-token rate, slab bands (e.g., 0-1M, 1M-10M), and per-route overrides; preview pane recomputes total cost for a selected time window in under 2s for typical accounts
Attribution UI highlights primary cost drivers with pre-computed deltas (model change, prompt length, route volume) and links to prompt set examples used for regressions
Design spec includes responsive rules for widths, truncation, and tooltip behavior; engineering handoff includes token-count sampling strategy to prevent UI slowdowns
Accessibility: table and export controls meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard navigation patterns
Prototype reviewed by PM and Eng and accepted for implementation or a clearly documented list of follow-ups
